title: Latency topology observability harness
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end observability harness that produces p95/p99 latency telemetry and human-friendly dashboards across service endpoints (routes), model variants, and geographic zones (region/availability-zone). This ticket covers the ingestion pipeline, aggregation topology, dashboard widgets, regression detectors, and a small load-test playback integration so product teams can validate latency baselines for new model rollouts.

Scope:
- Add a new aggregation key schema: service_route | model_variant | region_zone | env_tag.
- Emit streaming percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec per minute into the telemetry pipeline with stable histograms and TTL for short-term (1h) and baseline (30d) windows.
- Implement a topology-aware rollup layer that can compute cross-region comparisons without double-counting burst traffic.
- Provide a dashboard template with: heatgrid (routes x models), region sparklines, percentile trend lines, and an interactive regression inspector that surfaces suspected regressions with sample traces and request metadata.
- Integrate a small playback harness that replays captured request traces at configurable RPS to validate quantile changes under load.

Non-goals (this ticket): automated rollback actions, full-blown canary orchestration, or long-term cold storage optimizations. Those will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry emits p50/p95/p99 and tokens_per_sec for every request with aggregation keys: route, model, region; sample rate configurable per-route
Aggregation layer produces 1m and 5m rollups and a 30d baseline summary accessible via the metrics API
New dashboard shows heatgrid across top 200 routes and allows slicing by model and region; clicking a cell opens regression inspector
Regression detector flags changes in p95/p99 exceeding configurable percentage or absolute thresholds and generates a concise alert with example traces
Playback harness can replay a stored 15-min trace at up to 500 RPS in staging and produce comparable quantile outputs
implementation_notes: Use existing histogram format used by runtime-metrics to avoid schema churn; add 'aggregation_key_v2' with route+model+region concatenation
Prefer client-side prefix tagging for route/model where available to reduce server-side enrichment load
Aggregation service will maintain sliding-window mis-weights to prevent burst amplification across rollups
Regression detector will run nightly on baseline vs. last-24h with a two-stage filter: statistical significance (bootstrap) then practical delta (>10% p95 or >50ms)
Playback harness will reuse inferbench framework, extend it to rehydrate KV-cache where trace contains warm-up requests
testing_plan: Unit tests for aggregation-key generation and histogram ingestion
Synthetic load runs in staging comparing current p95/p99 to baseline for control model and heavy-model (quantized) variants
E2E test: deploy dashboard to staging, run playback harness, validate that regression detector alerts on injected latency increases
Manual QA: PM/Design review of dashboard UX, verify drilldowns and trace links to tracing system
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable telemetry for 10 canary routes, run playback to validate metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (internal): enable for all staging routes and expose dashboard to platform + PMs (1 week)
Phase 3 (gradual prod): opt-in deployment for 10% of prod routes, monitor false positive rate of regression detector before wider rollout (2 weeks)
Phase 4: full rollout and retro with metrics on detection precision and dashboard usage
risks: Telemetry volume increase may spike ingestion costs if sample rates are high; mitigate with adaptive sampling per route
False positives from regression detector could cause alert fatigue; need tuned thresholds and manual whitelist
Playback harness may not perfectly reproduce multi-tenant KV-cache warm states leading to mismatched p95; document limitations
Dashboard heatgrid for >10k routes could be slow; will provide top-N default and on-demand lazy queries
